name: setresgid32
synopsis: int setresgid32(gid_t rgid, gid_t egid, gid_t sgid);
description: Sets the real group ID, effective group ID, and saved set-group-ID of the calling process. An unprivileged process can only set these to the current real GID, effective GID, or saved set-group-ID, while a privileged process can set them to arbitrary values. If an argument is -1, the corresponding ID is not changed, and the filesystem GID is always set to the effective GID.

parameters.name: rgid
parameters.description: The new real group ID, or -1 to leave unchanged

parameters.name: egid
parameters.description: The new effective group ID, or -1 to leave unchanged

parameters.name: sgid
parameters.description: The new saved set-group-ID, or -1 to leave unchanged

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The call would change the caller’s real GID (i.e., rgid does not match the caller’s real GID), but there was a temporary failure allocating kernel data structures or it would exceed the RLIMIT_NPROC resource limit.
One or more of the target group IDs is not valid in this user namespace.
The calling process is not privileged (lacking the CAP_SETGID capability in its user namespace) and tried to change the IDs to values that are not permitted.
